nodes neither of which is an ancestor of the other in TD.) (II) For every edge (u,v) of G, if u is at depth i and v is at depth j in TB, then |i-j|=1. Which of the statements above must necessarily be true?
questions.explanation: Checking each statement: - (I): in DFS of an undirected graph, every non-tree edge joins a vertex to its ancestor (back edge); cross edges cannot occur True - (II): in BFS, an edge can join two vertices at the same depth (e.g. a triangle), so |i [latex]-[/latex] j| can be 0 False Answer: I only Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
questions.explanation_html:

- (I): in DFS of an undirected graph, every non-tree edge joins a vertex to its ancestor (back edge); cross edges cannot occur True
- (II): in BFS, an edge can join two vertices at the same depth (e.g. a triangle), so |i [latex]-[/latex] j| can be 0 False

Answer: I only
